source.creator: AI Revolution

normalization.overview: AI Revolution’s public title declares an AI singularity. A private machine transcript suggests a Jack Clark IMF attribution; the first-party benchmark and economic scenarios warrant narrower conclusions.
normalization.whyItMatters: Useful to people setting research or workforce plans who need to separate measured agent performance from a conditional 2030 scenario. Watch the benchmark and scenario explanations; skip the headline as a decision rule.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: The paper shows strong performance on bounded calculations, not open-ended scientific discovery. The $44.4 trillion figure is the extreme branch of a model. Use these as inputs for reversible stress tests, with explicit assumptions and human authority.
normalization.falsification: Revise the benchmark assessment if independent reruns and broader discovery tasks support a different capability claim. Revise the economic call when observed adoption, displacement and GDP data discriminate among the model scenarios.
normalization.freshness: Primary benchmark and scenario sources checked 2026-10-19. The IMF singularity attribution remains unverified; 2030 results are conditional, not observed.

claims.proposition: Jack Clark declared at an IMF lecture that the technological singularity has already arrived.
claims.assessment: A private machine transcript suggests an indirect paraphrase. Exact video audio and first-party Clark wording remain unverified.
claims.limits: A Reuters account of rapid AI progress is not a lecture transcript and cannot establish Clark’s exact wording.
claims.temporalScope: Source and linked reports checked 2026-10-19; model and economic conditions may change.

claims.proposition: GPT-6 Astra solved 49 of 50 unpublished TheoPhysEval physics problems in the authors’ realistic agent track.
claims.assessment: The benchmark authors report 98% for the Astra plus Codex harness.
claims.limits: One run, 50 selected problems and grading ambiguities limit generalization. GhostMesh has not rerun the evaluation.
claims.temporalScope: Source and linked reports checked 2026-10-19; model and economic conditions may change.

claims.proposition: The TheoPhysEval score demonstrates solutions to breakthrough open problems in physics.
claims.assessment: The paper explicitly says its tasks are not breakthrough open problems and do not require construction of new physical theories.
claims.limits: Strong performance on bounded calculations remains important; it is a different result from original discovery.
claims.temporalScope: Source and linked reports checked 2026-10-19; model and economic conditions may change.

claims.proposition: Unpublished benchmark answers mean the agents could not rely on memorized physics literature.
claims.assessment: Unpublished answers reduce direct answer contamination, but the paper says the small isolated-track change suggests significant memorization of relevant literature.
claims.limits: This does not prove any specific answer was copied. It limits any categorical exclusion of memorization.
claims.temporalScope: Source and linked reports checked 2026-10-19; model and economic conditions may change.

claims.proposition: Anthropic’s extreme scenario yields US GDP of $44.4 trillion in 2030, 32.4% above its no-AI baseline.
claims.assessment: Anthropic’s public scenario explorer gives these values at 2025 prices and specifies demanding capability and adoption assumptions.
claims.limits: This is one conditional modeled path, not Anthropic’s prediction or a measured effect.
claims.temporalScope: Source and linked reports checked 2026-10-19; model and economic conditions may change.

claims.proposition: The United States is forecast to reach $44.4 trillion GDP in 2030 because of AI.
claims.assessment: Anthropic presents $44.4 trillion as its extreme case alongside $34.1 trillion modest and $36.3 trillion substantial cases.
claims.limits: The model omits policy responses, business cycles and some demand effects; actual outcomes may differ materially.
claims.temporalScope: Source and linked reports checked 2026-10-19; model and economic conditions may change.

claims.proposition: The extreme scenario produces unusually high knowledge-worker displacement and a lower labor share.
claims.assessment: The CEPR authors describe nearly one in five cognitive workers unemployed in the extreme case and a labor share decline from about 60% to 45%.
claims.limits: These are modeled conditional outcomes, not current layoffs or a point forecast.
claims.temporalScope: Source and linked reports checked 2026-10-19; model and economic conditions may change.

claims.proposition: A single extreme scenario is enough to justify irreversible staffing or infrastructure decisions now.
claims.assessment: GhostMesh rejects this decision rule because the source offers distinct paths and explicitly says the future is not predetermined.
claims.limits: A reversible stress test could still be useful; it requires an organization-specific baseline and human review.
claims.temporalScope: Source and linked reports checked 2026-10-19; model and economic conditions may change.

references.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
references.author: A. Ramesh Chandra and coauthors
references.location: Abstract; sections II–V, especially problem selection, grading and discussion
references.independence: The authors report one run of their own 50-problem evaluation. Their score is not an independent replication or a test of breakthrough research.

references.title: Scenarios for our Economic Future
references.author: Anthropic Economics team
references.location: Three scenarios; GDP, employment and model limitations
references.independence: The model authors expose assumptions and caveats. The scenarios are conditional illustrations, not observed 2030 outcomes.
references.dateNote: The public explorer states v1.0, September 2026; no day is shown on the page.

references.title: Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI
references.author: Anton Korinek, Chad Jones, Szymon Sacher, Tess Cotter and Peter McCrory
references.independence: This is the same research family as Anthropic’s explorer, not an independent replication of the model or forecast.

relationships.reason: The physics benchmark reports 49 of 50 bounded calculations; the paper examines expert judgments about contributions to two open-ended research questions. Compare what a task score and a research judgment establish without treating either as a test of the other.

normalization.relationshipDisposition: One topic-level route contrasts a bounded physics benchmark with expert judgment of open-ended research. Neither Reader corroborates or rebuts the other's measured result.

relationshipReview.rationale: The physics benchmark and research-evaluation paper measure different constructs. Their one link invites comparison without treating a bounded score as research judgment. Reassessed against the new local AI Reader; no additional cross-source claim or substantively distinct route was established. The new Anthropic source-control Reader was assessed for this updated catalog; existing edges remain unchanged. Reassessed against four distinct AI Engineer video theses; their new outgoing links carry the qualified comparisons, with no new outgoing edge warranted from this existing entry. The HORTRAME visual swarm Reader was assessed as a new catalog neighbor; no additional outgoing route is justified by its distinct film and mathematics source. The newly added DeepInfer source was checked for another outgoing route; none is justified beyond its new Reader-to-Reader routes. The new Hassabis profile was compared for a specific shared claim; no further typed relation is admitted on thematic overlap alone. Compared the new Orca fleet Reader as a possible target; its three outbound comparisons cover the supported links, and no reciprocal claim of source corroboration is warranted.
